items.headline: Bondi Sushi to Open at Rockefeller’s 1221 Avenue of the Americas
items.summary: Ah, salmon skin roll . New York and Miami-based Japanese restaurant brand Bondi Sushi has leased 4,400 square feet at Rockefeller Group ’s 1221 Avenue of the Americas in Rockefeller Center , the property owner announced Monday. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space in Manhattan’s nearby Plaza District along Fifth Avenue between 49th and 59th streets was $2,471 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data.…

items.headline: Got Your Six Cannabis Dispensary Secures Manhattan Flagship
items.summary: A cannabis store is opening its Manhattan flagship location at the base of a luxury Tribeca condominium building. Got Your Six , a licensed dispensary based in New Jersey, has signed a 2,300-square-foot lease at 256 West Street , also known as 92 Laight Street . The corner retail lease between Laight and Vestry streets occupies part of the ground floor at Riverloft Condominiums , a 13-story luxury complex, and is near Hudson River Park . Crain’s New York first reported on the deal.…

items.headline: JLL: Retail Vacancy Dips to 4.3% as Openings Beat Closures
items.summary: U.S. retail net absorption totaled 8.3M SF in Q3 after 10.2M in Q2, and vacancy slipped to 4.3%. Over 12 months the market absorbed 24.4M SF, versus a 7.0M SF loss a year earlier. Discount, off-price, grocery, fitness and entertainment tenants are backfilling boxes left by the 2024-2025 bankruptcy wave, often at higher rents. Net new supply is only 0.25% of inventory. Asking rents are up 1.8% against 3.7% inflation.…

items.headline: Financial Tech Platform Intuit Takes 4K SF at the Orchard in LIC
items.summary: The Orchard , Queens’ tallest residential tower, has signed several new retail leases totaling 7,468 square feet, building owner and developer BLDG Management announced Thursday. In September, financial services platform Intuit , the company behind programs including TurboTax , QuickBooks , Credit Karma and Mailchimp , signed a 3,546-square-foot lease at the 70-story property at 42-06 Orchard Street in Queens’ Long Island City neighborhood.…

items.headline: Banks Lock Up Manhattan Retail Space as Availability Hits Low
items.summary: Bank of America took 16,000 square feet at 19 Union Square West and Citibank took 14,000 square feet at 170 West 72nd Street, two of Manhattan’s largest third-quarter retail leases. Most bank activity is renewals and strategic relocations by existing tenants, and banks are returning to corner locations in a market where space is hard to replace. Prime corridor availability fell to a record-low 157 spaces, and one JLL broker has five or six more bank deals in progress, a sign of broader retail strength.…

items.headline: CVS Split Would Create Two Public Companies by 2028
items.summary: CVS Health plans to separate into a healthcare solutions company and a retail pharmacy company, with the split expected to finish in the first half of 2028. The healthcare company keeps the CVS Health name and brands including Aetna and Caremark, while CVS Pharmacy will operate roughly 9,000 stores, MinuteClinic and mail pharmacy. A standalone 9,000-store retail tenant matters to net lease owners, though the announcement coverage gives no detail on how leases or guarantees will be handled.…

items.headline: Retail Net Absorption Hits 9.6M SF in Q3
items.summary: U.S. retail net absorption reached 9.6 million SF in Q3, the fifth consecutive positive quarter, led by neighborhood, community and strip centers at 2.4 million SF. Completions hit a quarterly low of 5.5 million SF and a record-low four-quarter total of 7.4 million SF, keeping availability at 4.8% and lifting asking rents 2.5%. Leasing is strong but investment volume fell 6% to $16.8 billion, so landlords hold pricing power while buyers stay cautious on asset-level pricing. Key Takeaways U.S.…

items.headline: First Washington’s Alex Nyhan on Grocery-Anchored Retail
items.summary: Guest: Alex Nyhan, CEO, First Washington Realty Alex Nyhan is CEO of First Washington Realty, one of the largest owners and operators of grocery-anchored and neighborhood retail in the country, with nearly 150 shopping centers across 22 states. He joined the company in 2014 after stints as a special assistant in the mayor’s office in Washington, DC, and at Forest City Enterprises, where he worked on a 42-acre waterfront redevelopment on the Anacostia River.…

items.headline: Simon Property Raises 2026 FFO Guidance After 4.7% Q3 Gain
items.summary: Real Estate FFO rose 4.7% to $1.277 billion, or $3.37 per share, in Q3, and Simon lifted full-year guidance to $13.30 to $13.40 per share, up $0.10. Occupancy reached 96.5% in U.S. malls and Premium Outlets, base minimum rent rose 6.1% to $62.75 per SF, and reported retailer sales climbed 14.8% to $852 per SF. Net income fell to $1.54 per share from $1.86 on $99.6 million of non-cash losses, while the dividend rose 4.5% to $2.30 and Simon repurchased $236.5 million of its stock.…

items.headline: VNS Health Renews 8K-SF Lease at the Bronx’s Hutchinson Metro Center
items.summary: VNS Health , formerly known as the Visiting Nurse Service of New York, has renewed its 8,000-square-foot lease for its regional office at 1200 Waters Place in the Morris Park neighborhood of the Bronx, property owner Simone Development Companies announced Wednesday. The senior care and in-home nursing provider has been a tenant at the mixed-use property since 2003.…

items.headline: Sports Clothing Brand RBX Direct Signs 5K-SF Garment District Lease
items.summary: An activewear brand has signed a lease for an office and showroom in Manhattan’s Garment District. RBX Direct took 4,800 square feet at Lal Sani ’s 102 West 38th Street , where asking rent was $35 per square foot, according to landlord broker Adams & Company . Adams & Company did not disclose the length of the lease or the name of the landlord, but the most recent filings in property records show the building has not traded hands since 1994 when it was purchased by Sani.…

items.headline: Sui Yoga to Open 13K-SF Studio at 71 Fifth Avenue
items.summary: Wellness and fitness operator Sui Yoga has selected 71 Fifth Avenue for its second Manhattan location. The hot yoga, Pilates and strength training studio inked a 13-year deal for 13,000 square feet at the Midtown South building, located one block west of Union Square at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 15th Street. Asking rent was $1.7 million per year. The deal involved the property’s previous landlord, Madison Capital , as well as its new owner.…

items.headline: Apparel Brand American Giant Leases Brooklyn Store at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue
items.summary: San Francisco-based apparel brand American Giant has arrived in Brooklyn. The manufacturer of sportswear and casual clothing made exclusively in the United States has signed a lease for 3,400 square feet at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue in North Williamsburg, where it will open its first Brooklyn store, according to a source familiar with the deal.…
